subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type, TPS targets, concurrency, token mix
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@edgehealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up & next steps

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet you and Amit. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated properly:

Summary of what you shared
- Target deployment mode: Dedicated capacity to start; evaluating Private VPC for Q4.
- Primary workload: mixed chat + generation (employee-facing summarization + customer support), plus embeddings for search reranking.
- Peak requests: ~200 requests/sec (RPS) during US business hours; sustained average ~60 RPS.
- Concurrency: expected 40 concurrent active requests during peaks; some long-tail streaming sessions (~50 concurrent low-rate streams).
- Token profile (per request): prompt ~40 tokens, completion ~120 tokens on average; spikes up to 1,500 tokens for long reports (rare).
- Preferred models: Llama-3 13B (open), but willing to test 70B variant for higher-quality summaries if cost allows.

Questions we still need from you
1) Percent split by request type (chat/generation vs embeddings) across total RPS.
2) SLA/latency targets for 95th percentile — is 250ms acceptable for short chats, or do you need <150ms?
3) Any hard constraints on quantization or model variants (e.g., must be FP16/Half vs can use q4_0)?
4) Procurement timeline / PO cadence (we typically need 4–6 weeks for Dedicated onboarding once PO is in).

Next steps from Redwood
- I'll sketch two sizing options (cost-optimized vs latency-optimized) with recommended GPU types (A100 vs H100), estimated throughput, and a short rollout plan.
- Attached is a quick sizing template — please fill the split (%) for embeddings vs chat and confirm latency SLO.

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (fill & return)

I'll follow up with sizing options by Monday. Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up & next steps

Thanks Aditya — quick answers below (filled the template, attached):

- Split: ~70% chat/generation, 30% embeddings.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile should be <= 200ms for short (<=512 token) responses.
- Quantization: open to q4_0 for non-critical models; for model variants used in clinical summarization we need to avoid quality regressions — happy to validate.
- Peak behavior: 200 RPS peak with ~40 concurrent; spikes to 260 RPS during certain reports.
- Timeline: PO likely in mid-July; pilot in August if sizing matches.
- Models: Starting with Llama-3 13B for pilot; evaluate larger 70B for summaries in Q4.

Attached: completed dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx

—Priya

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@edgehealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@edgehealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing options (2 proposals)

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the completed template — very helpful. Based on your inputs I sketched two pragmatic options below (high-level — final will include cost/quoting):

Option A — Latency-optimized (recommended if you need tight 95p SLAs)
- Hardware: 4x NVIDIA H100 (80GB) nodes
- Expected sustained throughput: ~180–220 RPS for Llama-3 13B (depending on batching)
- Concurrency: supports ~40 medium-latency concurrent requests with P95 ~150–200ms for <=512 tokens
- Pros: best single-request latency, good headroom for spikes
- Cons: higher monthly commit cost

Option B — Cost-optimized
- Hardware: 8x NVIDIA A100 (80GB) nodes (larger pool, denser batching)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~220–300 RPS for Llama-3 13B when batching is effective
- Concurrency: handles larger batch-driven throughput; P95 for short responses ~200–300ms
- Pros: lower $/token when workload is batchable and embeddings are offloaded
- Cons: slightly higher P95 latency on short chat paths

Notes & assumptions
- All estimates assume q4_0 quantization for non-critical models; for clinical summarization we recommend FP16 until we validate quality.
- Embeddings workload will be routed to a separate pool (or scaled subset) to avoid blocking generation.
- Autoscaling: we can configure burst capacity (add 2–4 nodes) for short peaks; recommend a buffer for the 260 RPS spikes you mentioned.

Next steps
- I attached a draft proposal/quote — please review and let me know which option you'd like priced with a mid-July PO timeline.
- Marissa will follow up with formal pricing details and SLA language.

Attachments: edgehealth-dedicated-proposal.pdf

Thanks,
Aditya
